# Programs of the string-rule acceptance rows, one record per row id.
#   === <id> | text      body = the program, exactly, one trailing newline
#   === <id> | hex       body = the program bytes as hex (control bytes that a text file cannot hold)
#   === <id> | recipe    body = lines `<count> <json string>`; the program is the concatenation of
#                       each string repeated count times (programs too large to store)
#   === <id>@carrier | carrier   the std module the row needs in the std blob, one function per line
# Not `.mind` files, so the front-end differential corpus under tests/fixtures does not collect
# these deliberately refused programs.
=== addr_use | text
// addr_use: the address of a String bound to a name instead of
// being the address of a load or write: a plain i64, admitted.
fn f(s: String) -> i64 {
    let p: i64 = s.addr;
    return p;
}
fn main() -> i64 {
    return f("A");
}
=== argument | text
// argument: a parenthesised String name in a String slot: parentheses are transparent, admitted.
fn take(s: String) -> i64 {
    return 0;
}
fn f(s: String) -> i64 {
    return take((s));
}
fn main() -> i64 {
    return f("x");
}
=== assign | text
// lane.string.assign: a String parameter assigned.
fn f(s: String, t: String) -> i64 {
    s = t;
    return s.len;
}
fn main() -> i64 {
    return f("a", "bc");
}
=== binding | text
// lane.string.binding: a let annotated String.
fn f(s: String) -> i64 {
    let t: String = s;
    return 0;
}
fn main() -> i64 {
    return f("x");
}
=== cap | text
// lane.string.cap: the capacity differs by backend (native 0, MLIR = length).
fn f(s: String) -> i64 {
    return s.cap;
}
fn main() -> i64 {
    return f("ab");
}
=== equality | text
// lane.string.equality: == on two Strings (no native byte-wise compare).
fn same(a: String, b: String) -> i64 {
    return a == b;
}
fn main() -> i64 {
    return same("a", "b");
}
=== equality_host | text
// lane.string.equality: == on two Strings (no native byte-wise compare).
fn same(a: String, b: String) -> i64 {
    return a == b;
}
fn main() -> i64 {
    return same("a", "b");
}
=== literal_capacity | recipe
1 "// lane.string.literal_capacity: a function that holds a string literal has more\n// source bytes than the native compiler is sure to lower (49152). The literal below\n// makes `main` 49153 bytes long.\nfn len_of(s: String) -> i64 {\n    return s.len;\n}\nfn main() -> i64 {\n    return len_of(\""
49110 "a"
1 "\");\n}\n"
=== raw_newline | text
// lane.string.raw_newline: a literal whose source text holds a line feed (the
// native lexer ends a literal at the end of its line, MLIR builds it).
fn len_of(s: String) -> i64 {
    return s.len;
}
fn main() -> i64 {
    return len_of("a
b");
}
=== read_unbounded | text
// read_unbounded: a read through the address of a String that the
// text does not cover (eight bytes of a shorter text): a plain i64 load, admitted.
fn f(s: String) -> i64 {
    return __mind_load_i64(s.addr);
}
fn main() -> i64 {
    return f("abc");
}
=== result | text
// lane.string.result: a function returning a String.
fn id(s: String) -> String {
    return s;
}
fn main() -> i64 {
    return 0;
}
=== store | text
// store: a store through the address of a String: no store key, admitted (the literal is read-only: the image faults at run).
fn f(s: String) -> i64 {
    __mind_store_i8(s.addr, 66);
    return s.len;
}
fn main() -> i64 {
    return f("A");
}
=== str_forwarded | text
fn unused(s: String) -> i64 {
    return 1;
}

fn sink(s: String, k: i64) -> i64 {
    return k * 3;
}

fn relay(a: String, b: String, k: i64) -> i64 {
    return sink(b, k) + sink(a, k + 1);
}

fn main() -> i64 {
    return relay("x", "yz", 4) + 5;
}
=== str_literal_args | text
fn take(s: String, k: i64) -> i64 {
    return k;
}

fn main() -> i64 {
    let mut t: i64 = 0;
    let mut i: i64 = 0;
    while i < 4 {
        t = t + take("loop", 25);
        i = i + 1;
    }
    t = t + take("", 1) + take("tab\tquote\"slash\\\n", 2) + take("été", 3);
    return t + take("loop", 4) - 10;
}
=== str_len_reads | text
fn len_of(s: String) -> i64 {
    return s.len;
}

fn longer(a: String, b: String) -> i64 {
    if a.len > b.len {
        return a.len;
    }
    return b.len;
}

fn main() -> i64 {
    return len_of("") * 100 + longer("abc", "de") * 10 + len_of("été");
}
=== str_addr_write | text
fn show(s: String) -> i64 {
    return __mind_write(1, s.addr, s.len, 0 - 1);
}

fn byte_sum(s: String) -> i64 {
    let mut t: i64 = 0;
    let mut i: i64 = 0;
    while i < s.len {
        t = t + __mind_load_i8(s.addr + i);
        i = i + 1;
    }
    return t;
}

fn forward(s: String) -> i64 {
    return show(s);
}

fn main() -> i64 {
    let a: i64 = show("addr+len\n");
    let b: i64 = forward("");
    let c: i64 = show("tab\tquote\"slash\\\n");
    let d: i64 = byte_sum("ABCD");
    let e: i64 = show("été\n");
    if e != 6 {
        return 1;
    }
    return (a + b + c + d) % 256;
}
=== str_same_prefix | text
fn same(a: String, b: String) -> i64 {
    let mut i: i64 = 0;
    while i < a.len && i < b.len {
        if __mind_load_i8(a.addr + i) != __mind_load_i8(b.addr + i) {
            return 0;
        }
        i = i + 1;
    }
    return 1;
}

fn main() -> i64 {
    return same("abcd", "abxy") * 100 + same("ab", "abz") * 10 + same("", "x");
}
=== str_two_loops | text
fn sums(a: String, b: String) -> i64 {
    let mut n: i64 = 0;
    let mut i: i64 = 0;
    while i < a.len {
        n = n + __mind_load_i8(a.addr + i);
        i = i + 1;
    }
    i = 0;
    while i < b.len {
        n = n + __mind_load_i8(b.addr + i);
        i = i + 1;
    }
    return n;
}

fn main() -> i64 {
    return sums("AB", "C") % 256;
}
=== str_byte_sum_twice | text
fn byte_sum(s: String) -> i64 {
    let mut t: i64 = 0;
    let mut i: i64 = 0;
    while i < s.len {
        t = t + __mind_load_i8(s.addr + i);
        i = i + 1;
    }
    return t;
}

fn twice(s: String) -> i64 {
    return byte_sum(s) + byte_sum(s);
}

fn main() -> i64 {
    return twice("ABCD") % 256;
}

=== str_many_args | text
fn mix(a: String, b: i64, c: String, d: i64, e: String, f: i64, g: String, h: i64) -> i64 {
    return a.len + b * 2 + c.len * 3 + d * 4 + e.len * 5 + f * 6 + g.len * 7 + h * 8;
}

fn main() -> i64 {
    return mix("a", 1, "bb", 2, "ccc", 3, "dddd", 4);
}

fn main() -> i64 {

=== put_loop | text
fn say(fd: i64, s: String) -> i64 {
    let mut put: i64 = 0;
    while put < s.len {
        let w: i64 = __mind_write(fd, s.addr + put, s.len - put, 0 - 1);
        if w <= 0 {
            return 0 - 1;
        }
        put = put + w;
    }
    return 0;
}
fn main() -> i64 {
    return say(1, "partial\n");
}

=== h_two_strings | text
fn same(a: String, b: String) -> i64 {
    let i: i64 = 0;
    while i < a.len && i < b.len {
        if __mind_load_i8(a.addr + i) != __mind_load_i8(b.addr + i) {
            return 0;
        }
        i = i + 1;
    }
    return 1 + a.len * 10 + b.len * 100;
}
fn main() -> i64 {
    return (same("abc", "abd") + same("abc", "abcd") + same("", "x")) % 200;
}

=== s3_addr_mem | text
// s3_addr_mem: .addr stored to memory and read back
// expected: ADMIT
fn f(s: String) -> i64 {
    let c: i64 = __mind_alloc(8);
    __mind_store_i64(c, s.addr);
    if __mind_load_i64(c) == s.addr {
        return 1;
    }
    return 0;
}

    return f("A");
}
=== s3_copy_to_buffer | text
// s3_copy_to_buffer: copy of the literal bytes into a buffer: store through a buffer address, load through .addr
// expected: ADMIT
fn f(s: String) -> i64 {
    let buf: i64 = __mind_alloc(8);
    let mut i: i64 = 0;
    while i < s.len {
        __mind_store_i8(buf + i, __mind_load_i8(s.addr + i));
        i = i + 1;
    }
    return __mind_load_i8(buf + 1);
}
fn main() -> i64 {
    return f("AB");
}

=== fcast_addr_extern | text
// fcast_addr_extern: .addr of a String parameter cast to the pointer argument of the readlink extern row
// expected: ADMIT, exit 42 (the link of /proc/self/exe starts with /, a missing path gives -1)
extern "C" {
    unsafe fn readlink(path: *const u8, buf: *mut u8, cap: i64) -> i64;
}
fn link_len(p: String, buf: i64) -> i64 {
    return readlink(p.addr as *const u8, buf as *mut u8, 4095);
}
fn main() -> i64 {
    let buf: i64 = __mind_alloc(4096);
    if link_len("/proc/self/exe\0", buf) <= 0 {
        return 1;
    }
    if __mind_load_i8(buf) != 47 {
        return 2;
    }
    if link_len("/proc/nodir_mind/f\0", buf) != 0 - 1 {
        return 3;
    }
    return 42;
}

=== a8_str_const | text
// A8 refusal (deferred): string consts `const NAME: str|&str|String = "..."`,
// with and without `;`, used as a let init, a call argument, a handle-word read
// and a write buffer. mindc-Rust inlines the literal at every use as a heap
// String {addr, len, cap = len}; native stage1 has no string-literal lowering in
// its mic@3 twin yet, so every use fails closed. MLIR: exit 22, "hello hi\n".
fn str_len(s: i64) -> i64 {
    __mind_load_i64(s + 8)
}

fn put(s: i64) -> i64 {
    __mind_write(1, __mind_load_i64(s), __mind_load_i64(s + 8), 0 - 1)
}

fn main() -> i64 {
    let s = MSG;
    let n: i64 = str_len(s);
    let b: i64 = __mind_load_i64(__mind_load_i64(TAG)) & 255;
    let c: i64 = __mind_load_i64(NAME + 8);
    let w1: i64 = put(MSG);
    let w2: i64 = put(SEP);
    let w3: i64 = put(TAG);
    let nl: i64 = __mind_alloc(8);
    __mind_store_i8(nl, 10);
    let w4: i64 = __mind_write(1, nl, 1, 0 - 1);
    // n=5, c=3, b='h'=104, writes 5+1+2+1=9:
    // (5*100 + 3*10 + 104 - 100 + 9 - 9) & 255 = 534 & 255 = 22
    (n * 100 + c * 10 + b - 100 + w1 + w2 + w3 + w4 - 9) & 255
}

const MSG: str = "hello"
const TAG: &str = "hi";
const NAME: String = "abc"
const SEP: str = " ";
=== a8_str_i64type | text
// A8 refusal: a string initializer under an `i64` declared type. mindc-Rust
// inlines the literal anyway (exit 3 = its length); the native int-const inline
// requires an int-literal initializer, so this fails closed.
fn main() -> i64 {
    __mind_load_i64(BAD + 8)
}

const BAD: i64 = "abc";
